title: Eval-driven safety net for shadow and split traffic
creator: Ethan Park
description: Add an automated safety net that ties lightweight eval prompt sets to shadow and split traffic to detect quality regressions early and surface deterministic mitigation actions. The goal is not a single hard gate but a staged quarantine/fallback flow for split tests and shadow runs that reduces false positives across diverse customer prompt distributions.
acceptance_criteria: Instrument shadow traffic path to fork payloads to the eval harness without adding p99 latency to production path
Run per-deployment and per-customer evals on a configurable subset of prompt sets within 60s of request completion
Detect statistically significant regressions using permutation testing and signal a quarantine if regression persists across time windows
Quarantine action can be applied automatically to split weights or routed to safe-model fallback; actions are logged with reason and can be reversed via console
Dashboards show per-prompt and aggregate delta, alerting thresholds, and an audit trail for each quarantine/auto-action
steps: Design: define compact eval shard format (<=50 prompts) for shadow and split scenarios
Infra: add lightweight fork in runtime to copy request/response to eval pipeline asynchronously
Stats: implement non-parametric permutation test and bootstrap CI for small-sample prompts
Policy: build staged mitigation flow (notify -> weight-quarantine -> auto-fallback) with cooldown and hysteresis
UI: expose per-deployment eval config, observed deltas, and one-click rollback in Console
QA: end-to-end test using synthetic traffic and recorded customer sessions in staging
decisions: Use permutation testing (p-value + effect size) instead of simple z-tests to avoid parametric assumptions for skewed response metrics
Maintain per-customer baseline fingerprints to reduce false positives caused by customer-specific prompt distributions
Keep eval shards small and rotation-friendly so they can be updated without heavy rollout friction
Ship initial system as opt-in for Dedicated/Private customers and beta for hosted customers with >10k tokens/day
progress_updates: 2026-03-04 - Ethan Park: Drafted eval shard schema and minimal response metrics (semantic-similarity, token-entropy, banned-token-rate). Linked design doc.
2026-03-06 - Maya Thompson: Implemented async fork in dev runtime; verified no p99 regression on synthetic traffic. Created unit tests for payload copy and dedup keying.

2026-03-09 - DataSci (review): Prototype permutation test implemented; shows improved Type I control on skewed prompt sets. Suggested adding effect-size thresholds to avoid tiny but significant deltas triggering actions.
2026-03-11 - Maya Thompson: Wire up quarantine API (internal) and console prototype for engineers to trigger manual quarantine on staging deployments.
2026-03-12 - PM review (J. Alvarez): Approved pilot with three customers for beta. Added label for privacy review due to request copying across VPC boundary.
notes: This ticket focuses on early-detection and measured mitigation rather than aggressive automatic rollbacks. Aim is to reduce churn from false positives by combining per-customer baselines, non-parametric stats, and a staged quarantine policy. Follow-on work will integrate with eval scorecards and long-term golden-set management.
